heroHeadline: EU Expands Deportation Powers Citing ICE as Model; Newark Threatens GEO Lawsuit as Delaney Hall Detainees Strike
heroSubtitle: On June 2, 2026, Newark Mayor Ras Baraka threatened to expand the city's lawsuit against GEO Group — the private operator of Delaney Hall ICE detention facility in Newark — unless city officials are granted inspection access, as the facility's roughly 300 detainees remained on a hunger and work strike for over a week citing maggot-infested food, inadequate medical care, and non-functioning toilets. Newark Police assumed command from New Jersey State Police at Delaney Hall, and the overnight curfew (9 p.m.–6 a.m., half-mile radius) remained in force as Acting ICE Director David Venturella — himself a former GEO Group executive who oversaw the company's federal contracts at DHS — entered his second day in office. Separately on June 2, Dulce Consuelo Diaz Morales, a 22-year-old Maryland woman, received a U.S. passport — formally confirming that ICE had wrongfully detained her for 25 days in December 2025 despite her presenting a state birth certificate; DHS had previously asserted she 'is not a U.S. citizen.' The case, which went viral on TikTok, became a national example of risks from record-pace enforcement with reduced procedural safeguards. The Senate remained stalled on the $71.7 billion ICE/CBP reconciliation package — the largest single-year immigration enforcement investment in U.S. history — with Trump's June 1 signing deadline now formally missed and a floor vote unscheduled as Byrd Rule disputes persist. The 287(g) local enforcement partnership program has 1,882 enrolled agencies as of June 1 — up 174% since January 2025.
